native_result.query: How does the effect of increasing education expenditure on per capita GDP compare between developing countries and countries in Sub-Saharan Africa?
native_result.HypoA: The effect of increasing education expenditure on per capita GDP is more pronounced in developing countries outside of Sub-Saharan Africa compared to those within it
native_result.HypoB: Across 1975-2015, adjusted savings: education expenditure (% of GNI) is negatively associated with GNI per capita (constant 2015 US$) in raw levels, but that negative is a share-vs-base artifact because the exposure is a ratio to GNI, so the outcome sits in its own denominator. Restating exposure as an absolute per-capita education-savings flow (share x GNIpc) flips the LMC association positive (raw r=+0.958, detrended +0.622, differenced +0.506; lagged differenced elasticity +0.068 [-0.015,+0.150], p=0.109, T=38), while the same quantity for Sub-Saharan Africa is unidentifiable (n=5 levels / n=4 changes). The clearest group difference is on the input side: in LMC a rising education-savings share is associated with rising primary gross enrollment (+1.14 GER points per +1 percentage-point rise in the share, 95% CI [+0.25,+2.03], p=0.013, T=39), whereas in SSA no such association exists (-0.14 [-1.03,+0.74], p=0.753). I therefore hypothesize that the education-expenditure -> enrollment -> income association is observable but modest for developing (LMC) countries and effectively absent for SSA: SSA's enrollment expansion (primary gross 60.6 -> 98.0, secondary 14.8 -> 43.4) accelerated after its education share peaked at 6.10% in 1997 and fell to 3.15% by 2015 (primary +0.25 -> +1.33 pp/yr, secondary +0.41 -> +1.25 pp/yr), so SSA's enrollment gains are associated with something other than a rising education-expenditure share; over 2011-2015 SSA's per-capita education flow fell 9.23% while LMC's rose 7.94%, and SSA GNI per capita rose 5.08% versus 13.81% for LMC. In the primary differenced specification the cumulative LMC income elasticity is -0.297 [-0.724,+0.129] p=0.172, indistinguishable from zero, and the SSA income elasticity cannot be estimated from this file at all. Group-level aggregates only; no country-level inference; associations only, not causal effects; no GDP-per-capita series exists in the data.
native_result.WorkflowB: 1) Audited raw file (12x45; 2 groups x 6 series; 41 year columns) and produced the per-series/per-group percent-null table. 2) Melted 41 year columns to long, coerced blanks to NaN, mapped Series Code to short names, pivoted to an (group, year) x series analysis frame (82x8). 3) Stationarity diagnostics (ADF maxlag=2, AR1) established unit-root levels and stationary first log-differences, fixing differencing as the primary transformation. 4) Income leg on LMC only: level elasticity (labeled non-interpretable), primary first-difference-of-logs spec with lagged education regressors + linear trend + Newey-West 4, cumulative lag1-3 contrast with CI, reverse-causality probe, restricted 1991-2015 variant with LFPR and exports. 5) Enrollment leg (education savings -> primary and secondary gross enrollment) estimated in levels-with-trend and first differences for both groups, plus a Chow-style pooled group-by-savings interaction on 1991-2015 as robustness only. 6) Required denominator check: raw vs linearly-detrended vs differenced correlations, then reformulated exposure as an absolute per-capita flow to break the shared GNI base. 7) SSA income leg reported descriptively with explicit n=5 levels / n=4 changes and no p-values. 8) All coefficients registered with window, T, transformation and controls in out/results_master.csv.
